key_insight: Strong text-to-image generation may not require language pretraining. Halcyon learns from image–text pairs entirely from scratch, with its 0.52B model outperforming LlamaGen-XL/8 using 18.2× less pretraining compute.
problem_solved: Modern text-to-image systems typically depend on internet-scale language pretraining. This work tests whether that costly prerequisite is necessary for strong image generation.
method: Introduce Halcyon, a family of early-fusion multimodal autoregressive models.
Pretrain entirely from scratch on GPIC, a dataset of 100 million image–text pairs.
Compare generation quality and pretraining compute against existing text-to-image models.
impact: The results suggest a path to competitive text-to-image models without separately pretrained language components. For practitioners, this could simplify training pipelines and reduce pretraining compute requirements.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: 100M image–text pairs → Halcyon trained from scratch → generated images.
Quality bar chart: Halcyon-0.52B at 48.0 gFD versus LlamaGen-XL/8 at 63.3 gFD, labeled 'lower is better'.
Compute comparison badge highlighting '18.2× less pretraining compute' for Halcyon-0.52B.
Architecture sketch contrasting a pretrained-language-component pipeline with Halcyon's early-fusion approach.
paper_title: Text-to-Image Generative Modeling Without Language Pretraining
paper_authors: Keshigeyan Chandrasegaran, Yue Zhao, Armin W. Thomas, Ehsan Adeli, Jiajun Wu
